harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, cron access is now restricted to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow. The opsadmin user was created since it did not previously exist. Verified other users (e.g. antrieb) are denied crontab access while root/opsadmin succeed. Node1 was restarted via the mandatory protocol, and access control plus cron service health were confirmed intact post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 16.04), cron package (vixie-cron based), and confirmed no /etc/cron.allow or /etc/cron.deny existed initially
Created opsadmin user (uid 1001) since it did not exist on node1
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing 'root' and 'opsadmin' (owner root:root, mode 644), leaving /etc/cron.deny absent
Verified antrieb (a non-listed user) is denied crontab access with 'not allowed to use this program' error
Verified root and opsadmin can list/install/remove crontabs (installed and removed a test entry for opsadmin)
Captured baseline boot_id and cron service state for node1
Restarted node1 via 'sudo shutdown -r now' backgrounded so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned, confirmed boot_id changed proving an actual restart
Re-verified post-restart that cron.allow persisted, cron.service is active, and access enforcement (deny antrieb, allow opsadmin/root) still holds

evidence.requirement: Baseline: cron config/service state before any changes
evidence.summary: Confirmed Ubuntu 16.04 with vixie-cron installed, no existing cron.allow/cron.deny, cron.service active, and no opsadmin user present initially
useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsadmin succeeded, id shows uid=1001(opsadmin)

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin allowed to schedule cron jobs (config applied)
evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/cron.allow with 'root' and 'opsadmin', confirmed file contents and no cron.deny present

evidence.requirement: Proof that non-listed users are denied and listed users are permitted
evidence.summary: antrieb user explicitly denied ('not allowed to use this program (crontab)'); opsadmin and root allowed (crontab -l returns 'no crontab for X' not a permission error); opsadmin successfully installed and removed a live crontab entry

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity, cron service, config)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 2dffe735-a982-49f0-aa0a-19552507ae73, cron.service active, and /etc/cron.allow contents prior to restart
Backgrounded 'sudo shutdown -r now' returned 'reboot acknowledged' immediately

evidence.requirement: Node became unreachable then came back; changed boot identity proves real restart
evidence.summary: Connection refused immediately after reboot command, then exec succeeded again with new boot_id 66a01adf-057d-405c-a6b6-0d81c8e403ce (differs from pre-restart 2dffe735...)

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service and access-control enforcement
evidence.summary: After reboot: cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow still contains root/opsadmin, antrieb still denied crontab access, opsadmin still permitted
